records.gloss: For the director. A psalm of David.
pieces: For the music director. A psalm of David.

L.1: For the director: a psalm of David.

R.1: For the leader of the music. A song of David.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director
decisions.reason: As in 4:1.

decisions.choice: the last psalm of Book One
decisions.reason: Psalm 41 closes the first of the five books of the Psalms (Psalms 1-41). Like Psalm 1 it begins "How blessed", and verse 14 is the praise that ends the book.

records.heading: Betrayed by a friend, upheld by God

records.source: אַ֭שְׁרֵי מַשְׂכִּ֣יל אֶל־דָּ֑ל בְּי֥וֹם רָ֝עָ֗ה יְֽמַלְּטֵ֥הוּ יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: How blessed [is one who] gives thought to [the] weak; in [the] day of trouble YHWH will rescue him.
pieces: How blessed are those who care about the weak! When trouble comes, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will rescue them.

L.2: How blessed [is] the one who gives thought to the weak; in [the] day of trouble {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will rescue {{gender:them|him}}.

R.2: Life is truly good for people who care about the poor and the weak. When trouble comes, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will rescue them.

decisions.choice: How blessed
decisions.reason: As in 1:1.

decisions.choice: gives thought to: considers wisely and acts
decisions.reason: The verb (maskil) means to act with insight; here, to pay wise attention to the weak and help them (Proverbs 21:12).

decisions.choice: the weak: the poor, or those brought low by illness
decisions.reason: The word (dal) is the poor and powerless; in this psalm about sickness it may include the sick (verse 4).

decisions.choice: them, with "him" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word refers to anyone who cares for the weak.

decisions.choice: those, people (plural)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable speak of people in general, which needs no gender setting; the next verses go on in the plural.

records.source: יְהוָ֤ה׀יִשְׁמְרֵ֣הוּ וִֽ֭יחַיֵּהוּ וְאֻשַּׁ֣ר בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְאַֽל־תִּ֝תְּנֵ֗הוּ בְּנֶ֣פֶשׁ אֹיְבָֽיו׃
records.gloss: YHWH will guard him and keep him alive, and he will be called blessed in the land; and do not give him to [the] desire of his enemies.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will protect them and keep them alive; they will be counted blessed in the land. Do not hand them over to the will of their enemies!

L.3: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will guard {{gender:them|him}} and keep {{gender:them|him}} alive, and {{gender:they|he}} will be called blessed in the land; and do not give {{gender:them|him}} over to the desire of {{gender:their|his}} enemies!

R.3: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will protect them and keep them alive. People in the land will say how good their life is. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, do not let their enemies do what they want to them!

decisions.choice: and he will be called blessed: the word as read
decisions.reason: The words follow the form the Hebrew text's notes say to read, which begins with "and"; the written form differs slightly. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: do not give him: a turn to prayer
decisions.reason: In the middle of the promise the psalmist speaks to the LORD directly, asking him to do what is promised.

decisions.choice: the desire of his enemies: what they want for him
decisions.reason: The word is nefesh, here the appetite or will; compare 27:12.

decisions.choice: LORD,
decisions.reason: Readable names the one addressed (m2).

records.source: יְֽהוָ֗ה יִ֭סְעָדֶנּוּ עַל־עֶ֣רֶשׂ דְּוָ֑י כָּל־מִ֝שְׁכָּב֗וֹ הָפַ֥כְתָּ בְחָלְיֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: YHWH will sustain him on a couch of illness; all his bed you have changed in his sickness.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will hold them up on their sickbed; when they are ill, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} turn their whole bed of sickness to health.

L.4: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will sustain {{gender:them|him}} on a bed of illness; all {{gender:their|his}} bed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have turned over in {{gender:their|his}} sickness.

R.4: When they are sick in bed, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will give them strength. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will make them well again.

decisions.choice: all his bed you have changed: you restore him to health
decisions.reason: To turn or change the bed is to turn the sickness into health, so that the bed of illness becomes a place of rest. The past form states the hope as already done.

decisions.choice: you: the LORD addressed
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, the psalmist turns from speaking about the LORD to speaking to him.

decisions.choice: LORD,
decisions.reason: Readable names the one addressed (m2).

records.source: אֲֽנִי־אָ֭מַרְתִּי יְהוָ֣ה חָנֵּ֑נִי רְפָאָ֥ה נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י כִּי־חָטָ֥אתִי לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: I, I said, YHWH, be gracious to me; heal my soul, for I have sinned against you.
pieces: I said, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, show me grace! Heal me, because it is {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I have sinned against."

L.5: As for me, I said, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, be gracious to me; heal my soul, for I have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

R.5: I said, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please be kind to me. I have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Please heal me."

decisions.choice: I, I said: what I prayed in my own trouble
decisions.reason: The "I" is stressed. Having spoken of the one who cares for the weak, the psalmist now tells his own story: his prayer when he was sick.

decisions.choice: heal me, for I have sinned: sickness and confession
decisions.reason: He links his illness with his sin and confesses it (compare 38:4-5). The Bible does not say that every illness comes from the sick person's sin (John 9:2-3), but here healing begins with confession.

decisions.choice: me
decisions.reason: Nefesh here is the whole person (as in 6:5).

records.source: אוֹיְבַ֗י יֹאמְר֣וּ רַ֣ע לִ֑י מָתַ֥י יָ֝מ֗וּת וְאָבַ֥ד שְׁמֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: My enemies speak evil of me: When will he die, and his name perish?
pieces: My enemies say cruel things about me: "When will he die and be wiped from memory?"

L.6: My enemies speak evil about me: "When will he die, and his name perish?"

R.6: My enemies say mean things about me. They say, "When will he die? When will everyone forget him?"

decisions.choice: his name perish: he be forgotten
decisions.reason: A name lived on in a person's children and in the memory of others. For it to perish is to vanish without trace (9:6; 109:13).

decisions.choice: evil: malicious words
decisions.reason: The word (ra') is evil or harm: what they say wishes him harm.

records.source: וְאִם־בָּ֤א לִרְא֨וֹת׀שָׁ֤וְא יְדַבֵּ֗ר לִבּ֗וֹ יִקְבָּץ־אָ֥וֶן ל֑וֹ יֵצֵ֖א לַח֣וּץ יְדַבֵּֽר׃
records.gloss: And if [one] comes to see, falsehood he speaks; his heart gathers trouble for itself; he goes out to the outside, he speaks.
pieces: When any of them come to visit me, they say what they do not mean, while inside they gather up bad news; then they go out and spread it.

L.7: And if [one of them] comes to see [me], {{gender:they speak|he speaks}} empty words; {{gender:their|his}} heart gathers mischief for itself; {{gender:they go|he goes}} outside [and] {{gender:speak|speaks}} [of it].

R.7: When they come to see me, they pretend to be kind. But in their hearts they are looking for bad news about me. Then they go out and tell everyone.

decisions.choice: comes to see: a visit to the sick
decisions.reason: The visitor comes as if to comfort a sick man, but only to gather news to spread.

decisions.choice: falsehood, trouble: empty words and wicked news
decisions.reason: Falsehood (shav') is what is empty and untrue, as in 12:3; trouble ('aven) is wickedness or harm, here the bad news he stores up.

decisions.choice: they, their (with "he", "his" as the alternatives)
decisions.reason: The verse speaks of any one of the visitors.

decisions.choice: any of them, they (plural)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable speak of the visitors as a group.

decisions.choice: they pretend to be kind
decisions.reason: Readable says what the empty words are: false sympathy.

records.source: יַ֗חַד עָלַ֣י יִ֭תְלַחֲשׁוּ כָּל־שֹׂנְאָ֑י עָלַ֓י׀יַחְשְׁב֖וּ רָעָ֣ה לִֽי׃
records.gloss: Together against me they whisper, all who hate me; against me they devise evil for me:
pieces: All who hate me whisper together about me; they plot harm against me, saying,

L.8: Together against me they whisper, all who hate me; against me they devise harm for me, [saying,]

R.8: All who hate me whisper about me. They make evil plans against me and say,

decisions.choice: whisper: talk in low voices, perhaps cast spells
decisions.reason: The verb (lachash) is used of whispering and of the muttering of charmers (58:6; Isaiah 3:3). Here it is whispered talk against him.

decisions.choice: devise evil: what they say follows
decisions.reason: Their words follow in verse 9, so this verse ends with a comma.

decisions.choice: saying
decisions.reason: The Hebrew goes straight into their words; "saying" introduces them.

records.source: דְּֽבַר־בְּ֭לִיַּעַל יָצ֣וּק בּ֑וֹ וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁ֝כַ֗ב לֹא־יוֹסִ֥יף לָקֽוּם׃
records.gloss: A thing of worthlessness [is] poured out on him, and [now] that he lies down, he will not again rise.
pieces: "Some deadly thing has been poured into him; now that he is down, he will never get up again."

L.9: "A thing of worthlessness has been poured out on him, and now that he lies down, he will not rise again."

R.9: "Something terrible has taken hold of him. He is in bed now, and he will never get up again."

decisions.choice: a thing of worthlessness: a deadly disease, or a curse
decisions.reason: The word belial means worthlessness and ruin; it can describe deadly danger (18:5). "A thing" (davar) can also be "a word": they may mean a fatal illness or a curse that has fallen on him.

decisions.choice: now that he lies down: in his sickbed
decisions.reason: He lies sick, and they say he will never get up.

records.source: גַּם־אִ֤ישׁ שְׁלוֹמִ֨י׀אֲשֶׁר־בָּטַ֣חְתִּי ב֭וֹאוֹכֵ֣ל לַחְמִ֑י הִגְדִּ֖יל עָלַ֣י עָקֵֽב׃
records.gloss: Even a man of my peace, whom I trusted in him, who ate my bread, has made great against me [the] heel.
pieces: Even the friend I was at peace with, the one I trusted, who shared my bread, has turned his heel against me.

L.10: Even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, who ate my bread, has lifted up [his] heel against me.

R.10: Even my best friend has turned on me. I trusted him. He ate at my table.

decisions.choice: man of my peace: a close friend
decisions.reason: A man of one's peace (shalom) is a friend one lives on good terms with (Jeremiah 38:22).

decisions.choice: made great the heel: betrayed me
decisions.reason: The picture is uncertain: raising the heel to kick, to trip, or to walk away in contempt. All mean that a friend turned against him.

decisions.choice: who ate my bread: who shared my table
decisions.reason: To eat someone's bread was to share their hospitality and to be bound to them in loyalty. That makes the betrayal worse.

decisions.choice: John 13:18
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes this verse of Judas, who ate with him and betrayed him (John 13:18).

decisions.choice: has turned on me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m2).

records.source: וְאַתָּ֤ה יְהוָ֗ה חָנֵּ֥נִי וַהֲקִימֵ֑נִי וַֽאֲשַׁלְּמָ֥ה לָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you, YHWH, be gracious to me and raise me up, and I will repay them.
pieces: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, show me grace and lift me up, so that I can pay them back.

L.11: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, be gracious to me and raise me up, that I may repay them.

R.11: But {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please be kind to me. Make me well again, so that I can pay them back.

decisions.choice: raise me up: from my sickbed
decisions.reason: This answers the enemies' words, "he will not rise again" (verse 9).

decisions.choice: that I may repay them: justice, not private revenge
alternatives: that I may make it right with them
decisions.reason: If the speaker is the king, to repay is to bring the disloyal to account. The Bible elsewhere forbids taking revenge for oneself (Proverbs 20:22; Romans 12:19).

decisions.choice: Make me well again
decisions.reason: Readable says what raising up means here (m1).

records.source: בְּזֹ֣את יָ֭דַעְתִּי כִּֽי־חָפַ֣צְתָּ בִּ֑י כִּ֤י לֹֽא־יָרִ֖יעַ אֹיְבִ֣י עָלָֽי׃
records.gloss: By this I know that you delight in me: that my enemy does not shout over me.
pieces: This is how I know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are pleased with me: my enemy does not get to cheer in triumph over me.

L.12: By this I know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} delight in me: that my enemy does not shout in triumph over me.

R.12: Then I will know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are happy with me. My enemy will not win and cheer over me.

decisions.choice: shout in triumph: a war cry of victory
decisions.reason: The verb (rua') is the shout of an army that has won.

decisions.choice: I know: confidence in the answer
decisions.reason: He speaks as if the answer has come; the healing is the sign of God's favor.

records.source: וַאֲנִ֗י בְּ֭תֻמִּי תָּמַ֣כְתָּ בִּ֑י וַתַּצִּיבֵ֖נִי לְפָנֶ֣יךָ לְעוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: And I, in my integrity you have upheld me, and you have set me before your face forever.
pieces: As for me, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} keep hold of me in my integrity and let me stand before {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face for all time.

L.13: And as for me, in my integrity {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have upheld me, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have set me before {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face forever.

R.13: You hold me up, because my heart is true to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. You will let me stay with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forever.

decisions.choice: integrity: wholehearted loyalty
decisions.reason: The word (tom) is wholeness: a heart undivided toward God (7:9; 26:1). He has confessed his sin (verse 5); integrity is not sinlessness but sincerity.

decisions.choice: set me before your face: given me a place in your presence
decisions.reason: To stand before a king's face is to serve him and enjoy his favor (compare 11:7).

decisions.choice: because my heart is true to you
decisions.reason: Readable says what integrity means here (m1).

records.source: בָּ֘ר֤וּךְ יְהוָ֨ה׀אֱלֹ֘הֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מֵֽ֭הָעוֹלָם וְעַ֥ד הָעוֹלָ֗ם אָ֘מֵ֥ן׀וְאָמֵֽן׃
records.gloss: Blessed [be] YHWH, God of Israel, from the everlasting and until the everlasting. Amen and amen.
pieces: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, be blessed from ages past to ages to come! Amen and amen.

L.14: Blessed [be] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [the] God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Amen and amen.

R.14: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel! He has always been worthy of praise, and always will be. Amen! Amen!

decisions.choice: the praise that closes Book One
decisions.reason: Each of the first four books of the Psalms ends with a blessing of God like this one (72:18-19; 89:53; 106:48). It closes the book rather than only this psalm.

decisions.choice: Blessed be: praised
decisions.reason: To bless (barak) God is to praise and thank him.

decisions.choice: Amen: so it is, so be it
decisions.reason: Amen comes from the root of "firm, true". Said twice, it is a full agreement by all who hear (Nehemiah 8:6).

decisions.choice: He has always been worthy of praise, and always will be
decisions.reason: Readable says what the phrase means for the praise.
